exposure: ultrasound-guided suction evacuation for cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy (CSEP)
cohort: The study included ten women of reproductive age who presented with a cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy (CSEP) diagnosed by transvaginal ultrasound at King Abdullah Bin Abdulaziz University Hospital.
finding: Ultrasound-guided suction evacuation was found to be an effective, safe, minimally invasive, and reasonable approach for managing early cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy (CSEP) with minimal complications and a significant decrease in HCG levels.
followup_time: Patients were generally discharged on the same or following day, with HCG levels reaching undetectable; one case with partial molar pregnancy was undergoing follow-up until study publication.
